verdict.rationale: Riveter's own REST API and official SDKs let runs be started, polled, and paged headlessly, and webhooks return results without a UI, so it can be scripted into unattended automation. The evidence never documents a CLI or CI-specific usage, so the CI part of the story is only implied. Missing for 10: an official CLI, CI-pipeline documentation or examples (e.g., GitHub Actions or headless auth guidance), and independent or hands-on corroboration of headless/CI runs.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: The Riveter API lets you enrich data, build datasets, scrape webpages, quickly search the web, and extract data from complicated websites programmatically.
the SDKs handle auth, retries (429s and transient GET failures), the wait long-poll, polling until a run finishes (wait_for_result), and pagination
Official Go SDK for the Riveter API — enrich data, build datasets, scrape pages, and run web searches.
Prefer webhooks over polling: pass `webhook_url` on kickoff and Riveter POSTs the results to you when the run finishes.
